newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU upbraids eight of its own on green records.
newsitem.headline: EU upbraids eight of its own on green records.

text.p: The European Commission challenged eight EU countries on Monday over implementation of environmental rules intended to protect water quality, govern waste treatment and provide pollution data to the public.

Commission action, announced in three statements, included a welter of legal challenges before the European Court of Justice and the sending of several so-called reasoned opinions, the last stage before court action.

Greece, Belgium and Spain fell foul of the EU executive on waste, one statement said, prompting court action for the former's implementation of hazardous waste rules and for the others' failure to reduce toxic waste from discarded batteries.
In the same category, Luxembourg was also warned for shortcomings in its implementation of EU waste packaging rules.

Portugal, Greece and the Netherlands all face court action for alleged breaches of water rules, the first for its record on cleaning up urban waste water and the other two for not setting binding objectives for limiting various dangerous substances.
The Commission also warned Spain about its efforts to implement rules governing nitrate levels in farm run-off water.
Finally, the Commission warned Germany, Portugal, Italy, Greece and Spain for their failure to report the workings of their environmental freedom-of-information rules.
The Commission went a step further with Spain, challenging Madrid with a final warning over various aspects of its information laws, including fees levied for supplying data.

The Commission's multi-pronged court action, which comes after years of relatively patchy enforcement of EU environmental legislation, could lead to national capitals being ordered to step into line or face fines.
